observation.visible_scene: An indoor still-life view of a red-upholstered sofa against a pale wall, with two cream/white square pillows propped up. On the seat sit two glossy black octagonal pedestals, each topped by a reflective CD/DVD disc held in place by a small yellow conical hub at its center. The discs show iridescent rainbow reflections (a green streak and a magenta streak on the right disc, a bright radial glare and a thin edge mark on the left disc). The scene is essentially static throughout the excerpt.
visible_changes: Only slight handheld camera jitter is present: the framing of the two pedestals, the pillows, and the wall shifts by a few pixels and the viewing angle tilts minutely between frames, but the relative layout of objects does not change.
The specular/rainbow reflections on both discs move and re-brighten slightly as the viewing angle wobbles; this is a reflection change caused by camera motion, not by the discs themselves.

The radial edge-mark on the left disc and the green/magenta reflection bands on the right disc keep essentially the same orientation from the first to the last frame, so no clear disc rotation is observable.
The pillows, couch fabric, stands, and central hubs remain fixed in position; no object is added, removed, or displaced.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the discs were spinning before this segment or are spinning at a rate too slow/aliased to detect here.
Whether any person placed the discs or adjusted the camera; no operator is visible.
What happens after the last frame (the segment ends arbitrarily with the same static arrangement).
uncertain_details: The exact rotation state of the discs cannot be confirmed; the constant orientation of their marks/reflections suggests they are at rest, but a very slow or aliased spin cannot be ruled out.
The magnitude of camera motion is small and could partly be frame-to-frame noise rather than deliberate movement.
